admission_type.route_name: Luiss EU Test (Luiss Test) - admission via testing for EU/Schengen citizens
admission_type.test_or_certification: Luiss Test: psycho-aptitude questions inspired by the SAT model, assessing logical reasoning, problem-solving and mathematical skills. No minimum external test score is required; ranking is based on the Luiss Test result. Note: the exception that the Luiss Test is not valid for the Finance and Management programmes concerns master's degrees only and does not apply to this bachelor's programme.
admission_type.subject_area_group: Economics / Business (Business Administration is one of the four English-taught bachelor options, alongside Economics and Business, Global Law, and Management and Artificial Intelligence)

admission_type.route_name: Direct admission with certifications for non-EU/non-Schengen students
admission_type.test_or_certification: One of: SAT total score >= 1200/1600; LSAT total score >= 160/180; ACT total score >= 25/36; IB Diploma or IB Predicted Grade >= 36/45. Assessment also considers the documentation attached to the application and any assessment interview.
admission_type.number_of_choices_allowed: 1 (only one degree programme may be specified)
admission_type.subject_area_group: Economics / Business (Business Administration listed among the English-taught bachelor courses)

academic_requirements.prior_qualification: A valid upper secondary school diploma granting access to Italian universities, held or obtained by the deadlines set by the university.
academic_requirements.minimum_curricular_requirements: Not applicable - this is a bachelor's (first-cycle) programme; no ECTS/SSD curricular requirements apply.
academic_requirements.minimum_grade_or_gpa: No general minimum grade is published for the Luiss Test route. For the non-EU certification route, the minimum thresholds are the certification scores (SAT 1200, LSAT 160, ACT 25, IB 36). Country-specific minimum diploma averages apply separately (e.g. Albania: State Matura Diploma with a minimum average grade of 6.5).
academic_requirements.country_specific_rules: Luiss publishes a country-by-country list of qualifications eligible for enrolment, with country-specific minimum average grades and, in some cases, additional requirements (national entrance exams, extra school years). Qualifications are only accepted if obtained after at least two years of attendance in the same school system; qualifications awarded as part of a mobility programme are not eligible. The issuing and teaching institutions must both be accredited and recognised by the relevant ministry of education.
academic_requirements.document_recognition: For foreign qualifications, enrolment requires either a CIMEA Statement of Comparability or a Declaration of Value (DoV) issued by the competent Italian Embassy/Consulate, or an attestation of qualification where applicable; legalisation/apostille is required for compensatory-measure documents. Verification of the qualification is carried out by the Admissions Office at the enrolment stage, not at admission - an admitted candidate whose qualification does not comply cannot complete enrolment.
academic_requirements.compensatory_measures: If the qualification does not meet the prescribed guidelines, the applicant may compensate with either (a) completion of a Foundation Programme consistent with the intended field of study, lasting at least one academic year and issued by an accredited and recognised university, or (b) one full year of university/college studies at an accredited and recognised institution with all first-year exams passed. Such documents must be legalised and apostilled or accompanied by a CIMEA Statement of Comparability.

language_requirements.required_level: [uncertain] No explicit CEFR level or English certificate requirement is published for this bachelor's programme for the 2027/2028 cycle. English proficiency is effectively screened through the Luiss Test, which is taken in English for English-taught programmes. (By comparison, Luiss requires a B2 English certificate for its Foundation Programme, but that rule is not stated for direct bachelor admission.)
language_requirements.accepted_certificates: [uncertain] No list of accepted English certificates (IELTS / TOEFL iBT / Cambridge / Duolingo) is published on the 2027/2028 bachelor admission pages. To be confirmed when the admission notice is published from October 2026.
language_requirements.assessed_in_test: Indirectly yes: for degree courses taught in English the Luiss Test is administered in English, so English comprehension is required to sit the test. The test itself measures logical reasoning, problem-solving and mathematical skills, not language proficiency as a separate scored section.
language_requirements.exemptions: [uncertain] Not published for the 2027/2028 bachelor cycle.

entry_exam_or_test.test_name: Luiss Test (Luiss EU Test) for EU/Schengen citizens; for non-EU/Schengen citizens, no Luiss-administered exam - admission is based on an external certification (SAT, LSAT, ACT or IB)
entry_exam_or_test.content: Psycho-aptitude questions inspired by the SAT model, assessing logical reasoning, problem-solving and mathematical skills. Preparation materials, simulations and exercises are provided by Luiss on a dedicated page.
entry_exam_or_test.format: Online, via a platform specified by the university, with fairness controls including asynchronous audio-video verification tools and live proctoring.
entry_exam_or_test.dates: 2027/2028 a.y.: first session test administration 22-26 February 2027 (applications from October 2026 to 10 February 2027). A second session is announced but its dates are not yet published. Candidates may take part in more than one Luiss Test session in the same academic year.
entry_exam_or_test.fee: EUR 150 participation fee (same amount for the non-EU certification route)
entry_exam_or_test.language_of_test: English for this programme. Luiss states: for degree courses taught in Italian the test is taken in Italian; for those taught in English it is taken in English. Because the chosen degree course is indicated at application and is binding, the test language follows the programme choice. [uncertain] The 2027/2028 pages do not explicitly restate the rule that taking the test in English unlocks both English- and Italian-taught programmes while taking it in Italian restricts access to Italian-taught programmes; on these pages the binding single-programme choice determines the test language.
entry_exam_or_test.interview: EU test route: no interview mentioned. Non-EU certification route: 'any assessment interview' may form part of the Commission's evaluation, so an interview is possible but not guaranteed.

That page instead states a single binding degree-course choice whose language determines the test language. This is a conflict between the brief and the live source; the live source was followed.

Universitaly pre-enrolment and visa timetable are not described on the Luiss 2027/2028 non-EU admission page; only a general statement that obtaining a study visa is the candidate's responsibility. The Universitaly step derives from Italian national rules, not from a Luiss source.
